messages:
Alyssa: Heads-up — while testing qwen-mqa long-context (>=12k tokens) on canary, we see steady GPU memory growth attributed to KV pages not being reclaimed. Starts around token ~8k and climbs until OOM. :thinking:
Brad: Can you paste repro steps and which runtime/commit? Did we change any kernel selection or coalesce heuristics recently?
Alyssa: Repro steps: run `load-test --model qwen-70b-mqa --context 14k --rps 8 --batch-policy adaptive` against canary runtime v3.14.2 (deployed yesterday). Attached quick pmap snapshot: `pmap | grep kv_pages` shows page_count increasing from 5.2k -> 9.8k over 45m.
Cheng: run `kv-inspect --histogram --slot-info` on the same instance. If this is fragmentation we should see a lot of small free slots and a rising "window_unmapped" counter.
Marta: note: we merged the adaptive-batching tweak last week that allows heterogeneous-batch merging. That can cause ephemeral prefix thrash if KV reuse assumptions don't hold across seq-lengths. Could be interacting with MQA packing.
Alyssa: ran `kv-inspect` output (trimmed):
```
total_pages: 10240
resident_pages: 9876
free_runs: 1248
slot_sizes: [64, 128, 256, 512]
window_unmapped: 412
coalesce_ops: 37
last_eviction: 2025020312
most_common_slot: 256
```
Also `dmesg` shows no OOM killer, just allocation spikes.
Tomas: We switched the fallback kernel selector to `fallback_kernel_v2` in runtime v3.14.0 — that changed page allocation alignment (now 4KB -> 2KB affinity in some paths). That can increase fragmentation for models with large KV stride like Qwen. I filed a quick note in the PR: https://git.re/redwood/runtime/pulls/1278 (canary).
Brad: If fragmentation is worse under mixed MQA/GQA traffic, the kernel may be allocating many small fragments instead of coalescing. Can you capture a `kv-snap` (page id histogram) and `perf top` for 30s? Look for hotspots in `kv::alloc_page` and `slab_coalesce`.
Alyssa: `kv-snap` (snippet):
```
page_hist: {1: 3400, 2: 2200, 4: 1800, 8: 1200, hole: 450}
slab_free_ranges: 198
coalesce_attempts: 12
avg_contiguous_run: 3.2
```
When I forced `--sticky_batching=true` memory stabilized (resident_pages plateaued ~6k) but tail latency increased ~12% and throughput dropped ~8%.
Cheng: sticky batching reducing heterogenous merges is consistent: fewer mixed-length coalescence events -> less prefix eviction. For a mitigation, we can tune `min_coalesce_run` and `page_alignment` per-model. For qwen-mqa, aligning allocations to the rope stride (2048 tokens) reduces partial-slot waste.
Marta: quick mitigation before kernel fix: bump `min_slab_size` to 512 and set `coalesce_window_ms=5` for canary. That should prioritize larger allocations and give the GC sweep more time. We can flip flags via runtime flags: `--runtime.kv.min_slab=512 --runtime.kv.coalesce_window_ms=5`
Tomas: Agree; also add a telemetry counter to flag "rope_stride_mismatch" when allocation alignment != rope_stride. That will help triage other models. I'll add a small metric.
Alyssa: Kicking off an overnight run with those flags and sticky_batching off to preserve perf. Will post `perf` + final `kv-inspect` in the morning.
infra-bot: deploybot: Deployed runtime v3.14.2-canary to 3 nodes in us-west-2 :rocket:
Brad: Thanks — if this repros on canary, let's schedule a short rollback of fallback_kernel_v2 and run A/B with the alignment patch. If rollback stabilizes memory, we'll ship quick revert.
Cheng: Also adding a unit-test to the allocator fuzz harness to mix MQA/GQA-shaped KV streams and assert fragmentation < 10% after 1M ops.
Marta: Great. If Alyssa's overnight run looks good, let's roll mitigation flags to dedicated next. :thumbsup:
Alyssa: Will update tomorrow with the results. Thanks everyone! :pray:
